questions.question: Where is parking strictly prohibited?

options.text: In a loading zone, if you are not loading or unloading goods
In a parking bay with a time limit
In front of a petrol station

questions.explanation: Loading zones are reserved for vehicles actively loading or unloading goods. Parking there without a valid reason can obstruct businesses and delivery services.

questions.question: How far must you park from a pedestrian crossing?

options.text: 2 meters
5 meters
9 meters

questions.explanation: Parking too close to a pedestrian crossing reduces visibility for both drivers and pedestrians, increasing the risk of accidents.

questions.question: What is the maximum distance your wheels should be from the pavement when parking?

options.text: 200mm
450mm
1 meter

questions.explanation: Keeping your wheels within 450mm (45 cm) from the pavement prevents your car from obstructing traffic or posing a hazard to other road users.

questions.question: Why is parking near a fire hydrant prohibited?

options.text: It is only illegal in urban areas
It is an inconvenience for pedestrians
It prevents emergency services from accessing the hydrant

questions.explanation: Firefighters need quick and unobstructed access to fire hydrants in emergencies. A parked car could delay their response and worsen a fire situation.

questions.question: When are you allowed to park on a sidewalk?

options.text: If you are stopping for a short time
If no one is walking on it
Only if a sign specifically allows it

questions.explanation: Sidewalks are for pedestrians, and parking there forces them into the road, creating a safety hazard. It is only allowed if signs indicate it is permitted.

questions.question: How far must you park from an intersection?

options.text: 2 meters
5 meters
7 meters

questions.explanation: Parking too close to an intersection blocks the view of other drivers and pedestrians, increasing the risk of collisions.

questions.question: Can you park in front of a private driveway?

options.text: Yes, if it is your own driveway
No, because it blocks access for vehicles
Yes, as long as you leave space for a small car to enter

questions.explanation: Blocking a driveway prevents other vehicles from entering or exiting, which is a major inconvenience and could also be illegal.

questions.question: Under what condition can you park on a road narrower than 5.5 meters?

options.text: If you are driving a small car
If it is a one-way road
If there are no other cars around

questions.explanation: On a narrow road, parked vehicles can obstruct traffic. However, on a one-way street, cars all move in the same direction, reducing the chances of congestion.

questions.question: What should you check before parking in an area?

options.text: The condition of the road surface
If there is a road sign indicating parking rules
The colour of other parked vehicles

questions.explanation: Road signs indicate where parking is allowed, restricted, or prohibited. Ignoring them can lead to fines or your car being towed.

questions.question: Why should you avoid parking near a traffic light?

options.text: Because it may confuse other drivers
Because it makes the traffic light change slower
Because it is only illegal at night

questions.explanation: A parked car near a traffic light can block the view of the signal, causing drivers to react late or misunderstand the light changes.

questions.question: How close are you allowed to park to a fire hydrant?

options.text: 1 metre
1.5 metres
2 metres

questions.explanation: You must keep at least 1.5 metres away from a fire hydrant so that emergency vehicles can access it quickly in case of a fire. Parking too close could delay response time and put lives at risk.

questions.question: You are not allowed to park on a road that is narrower than ___ metres?

options.text: 10 metres
5,5 metres
7 metres

questions.explanation: Parking on roads narrower than 5.5 metres is normally not allowed because it can block traffic flow.
